ca_moon_goddess_arete.descent_text: The route ends on the back slopes of Temple Crag, and the summit is a short hike from the top if time allows. The way down is the standard Contact Pass descent: follow the back slopes to steep rock where a short rappel off fixed slings reaches Contact Pass. Below the pass, snow or loose scree and talus lead back to the lakes. Early in the season the snow below the pass can be kicked down or glissaded, but the scree and talus are loose and tiring.
ca_moon_goddess_arete.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Leave the trail near Second Lake, where most parties camp, and cross to the foot of the crag by scree slopes or the snowfield. From the base of the climb, traverse a ledge leftward to the buttress and scramble up a few hundred feet until the rock steepens; this is where the rope goes on. A good option is a snow chute running up the wall that lies between the Sun Ribbon and Moon Goddess aretes; crampons are useful early in the season.

ca_venusian_blind.descent_text: From the top of the arete, descend east on a climbers' trail toward Contact Pass. The trail turns into class 3 above the pass and then steepens to class 4 and 5 terrain, where most parties rappel from slings to the pass. Below the pass, snow can be glissaded and rock and scree lead back to the lakes. A rappel station on the left side of the arete higher up allows a short rappel into the gully, from which class 3 and 4 climbing reaches the summit plateau.
ca_venusian_blind.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Leave the trail near Second Lake and climb toward the base of the crag. Venusian Blind shares its start with Moon Goddess Arete: a snow chute between the Sun Ribbon and Moon Goddess aretes leads to a snow and rock traverse to the base. The snowfield is steep enough that crampons suit early season. Roughly 300 feet of third and fourth class leads to ledges, where Moon Goddess splits right and Venusian goes left; a short right-facing corner marks the start.
